findings.body:
**Verify the reviewer on the successful retry.**

In `test/ops/review/addressRerequestPersist.test.ts`, Lines 120-124 populate `reRequested` before the first request fails. Line 259 therefore passes even if the successful retry omits `octocat` or requests another reviewer. The fake still records `rerequest` for either case.

Record recipients separately for each successful request. Assert that the second invocation requests `octocat` before checking that the pending file was removed.

As per path instructions, “Prefer assertions that exercise intended behavior and its failure modes.”
findings.title: Verify the reviewer on the successful retry.

findings.body:
**Remove baseline carry-over across retries, and update the test that expects it.**

Doctrine I7 states that baseline values are never carried over by cache, and that a reused clean worktree re-probes its baselines. `makeAddressWorker` stores leg baseline results in `baselineCache`, keyed by parent SHA (`src/ops/review/addressWorker.ts:1089`). A later attempt with the same parent reads that cache. When a cached leg exists, `prepareBaseline` skips the leg `runChecks` call (`addressWorker.ts:1152-1164`). The test at `test/ops/review/addressWorker.baseline.test.ts:144` names this reuse as its expected behavior. Its assertion at line 163 expects the check-run count to be `'5'`, which depends on that skipped run.

Stop carrying leg baseline results across attempts. Each attempt must re-probe its baseline. Then recompute the expected count at line 163 from the re-probed behavior, and rename the test so it no longer describes cache reuse as expected.
findings.title: Remove baseline carry-over across retries, and update the test that expects it.

findings.body:
**Restructure the same-PR race test. The lock prevents the interleaving it tries to create.**

`removePrWorktree` and `resolvePrWorktree` both run their complete operation inside `withAdmission`, and both pass the same PR number. `withAdmission` runs the action inside `registry.withPrLock`, so the lock covers the whole invocation. While the removal's `worktree remove` call waits at the gate, `resolvePrWorktree` at lines 341-343 waits for the same PR lock. The gate is released only at line 345, which the test never reaches. If the removal enters the lock first, the test deadlocks and times out.

If the resolution enters the lock first, the test passes. In that case the removal does not park inside the locked region, so the intended in-lock re-load is not exercised.

An arrival signal from `gatedRun` does not fix this. The lock still prevents the two operations from overlapping. Remove the gate-based overlap. Create the fresh registration before the removal starts, or assert the serialized outcome in the order the lock enforces.

**Test-only deadlock risk:** the test can hang instead of failing fast, and it can pass without covering the stated interleaving.
findings.title: Restructure the same-PR race test. The lock prevents the interleaving it tries to create.
Build the successful-removal fixture paths from `REPO`, not the literal `/repo` path.
